Aaron was the bandleader of Those Lavender Whales and the founder of Fork & Spoon Records. Because Aaron always wanted to see his friends grow, we didn't just re-release an old circuit—we pushed ourselves to create something full of welcome surprises. The Preamp You’ve Been Asking For (And Then Some) For years, players have asked us to release the preamp section from our Parabola and Météore as a standalone pedal. At its core, the Aaron Graves Overdrive does exactly that: it makes small amps sound massive, pushes clean tube amps into natural breakup, and makes already-dirty amps sing. But we didn’t stop there. Dual Gain Stages: We added a second gain stage to our classic voicing, perfectly balancing the pedal's two distinct drive styles. Custom Bass Voicing Selector: Tailor your low-end response. COLORWAY Choose an option GREEN "BALTIM-ORANGE" Clear AARON GRAVES OVERDRIVE quantity Add to cart SKU: N/A Category: Pedals “Mostly I just want to see my friends grow.” We’ve had customers who just want our preamp from our "pawnshop" Parabola & Météore as its own pedal. It would have been a layup of a release. But Aaron always wanted to see his friends *grow*. So while on first glance this pedal looks like a straightforward overdrive/preamp, it has some surprises. Whether on its own or stacked with other drives, the Aaron Graves Overdrive brings both clarity and heft to the proceedings. And if it can get a bit gnarlier than people expected, we were reminded that Aaron learned guitar from learning Misfits songs. We heard people missed the “Mode B” circuit from our old Haymaker and Icarus V1 because it resembled power amp clipping. So we brought it back, but added a second gain stage to our classic voicing to balance the two drive styles more evenly. The bass voicing selector comes from listening to those of you who work in studios, love humbuckers, and/or like using the neck pickup. And there is PLENTY of gain and volume on tap. A portion of the sales proceeds from these pedals will go to Fork & Spoon Records, so that Aaron's friends may continue his work in creating music and community.
